items.title: Fahmi Fadzil offers condolences to families of four killed in LPT1 crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil expressed his condolences over the tragic accident in Temerloh that claimed the lives of four individuals, including a family of three, who were on their way back to Kuantan after attending the National Day celebration in Putrajaya. Through a post on Facebook, Fahmi also extended his condolences to the families of the victims who were killed in the accident, which also resulted in three others being injured in the collision involving 11 vehicles at Kilometre 110.4 of the East Coast Highway 1 (LPT1) (eastbound) in Lanchang, Temerloh, near the Temerloh Toll Plaza exit. The incident around 10 pm yesterday involved four cars, three sports utility vehicles (SUVs), a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), a pickup truck, one tanker truck and a bus.

items.title: Man accused of killing Charlie Kirk pleads not guilty to murder charge
items.summary: PROVO, Utah: Tyler Robinson, the man accused of fatally shooting prominent US conservative activist Charlie Kirk on a Utah college campus last year, pleaded not guilty on Tuesday to a murder charge that a judge ruled could carry the death penalty. That count carries the death penalty in Utah. He displayed pictures that he said showed Robinson created a "great risk of death" to others, with Kirk's security detail only feet away from Kirk when he was shot.

items.title: Putrajaya police seek man who sparked scuffle at National Day celebration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — Police urged a man suspected of sparking a disturbance during Monday’s 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya to turn himself in at the Putrajaya District Police Headquarters to assist with investigations. Putrajaya police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said police have received four reports regarding the incident so far. The incident is believed to have occurred yesterday (Aug 31) at 5 am,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Fire guts upper floor of 100-year-old pre-war shoplots in Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN: Fire destroyed the upper floors of two pre-war shoplots, including a clothing store, along Jalan Mahkota here late last night. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Mohd Razam Taja Rahim said a distress call was received at 11.33pm, prompting a response from the Kuantan fire station. 43, a clothing shop.

items.title: 'Discomfort' at G20 finance talks as US hosts Russian minister
items.summary: ASHEVILLE, US: The Russian finance minister's presence at US-hosted G20 talks has cast a shadow over the gathering, as Washington pushed Tuesday to rally support from partners on Iran sanctions and on reducing trade imbalances. Finance ministers and central bank governors from the Group of 20 major economies are holding two days of talks that end Tuesday in Asheville, North Carolina. But the US-Israel war with Iran, President Donald Trump's tariffs and the in-person attendance of Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov – despite Moscow's 2022 invasion of Ukraine – weighed on the group's work.

items.title: Anwar calls for answers in 11-vehicle crash on LPT1 that killed four including family on way home from N-Day parade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for a thorough investigation into the accident in Temerloh that claimed the lives of three members of a family returning from the National Day celebrations in Putrajaya. Four people, including three family members, were killed and three others injured in a collision involving 11 vehicles at KM110.4 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT) 1 eastbound, near the Temerloh Toll Plaza exit in Lanchang, Temerloh, at about 10 pm Monday. The accident involved 11 vehicles, comprising four cars, three sports utility vehicles (SUVs), a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), a pickup truck, a tanker lorry and a bus.

items.title: Ringgit opens lower vs greenback amid higher oil prices, Fed rate hike bets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Wednesday amid higher Brent crude oil prices, which heightened inflation concerns, boosting expectations of a US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike, said an analyst. Mohd Afzanizam said fears of higher inflation and a higher chance of a Fed rate hike had bolstered the value of the US dollar. "The US dollar index (DXY) rose 0.25 per cent to 99.677 points as the odds of a higher US interest rate in the September Federal Open Market Committee meeting rose to 65 per cent," he told Bernama.

items.title: Asian markets tumble as US-Iran fighting lifts oil and bond yields
items.summary: MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 0.8 per cent in early trading as South Korea's KOSPI dropped three per cent on the open and Japan's Nikkei 225 sank 2.2 per cent. Brent crude futures extended gains into a second day as trading resumed in Asia, rising 0.7 per cent to US$95.34 a barrel after the US launched a barrage of airstrikes on Iran on Tuesday, which earlier pushed oil prices to a five-week high. Gold was flat at US$4,328.59 an ounce, while bitcoin slipped 0.2 per cent to US$77,246.57 and ether was 0.3 per cent lower at US$2,412.60.

items.title: Penang ferry crash: 21 injured in collision near Sultan Abdul Halim Terminal
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 2 — A ship collided with a Penang ferry near the Sultan Abdul Halim Ferry Terminal (PSAH) last night, injuring 21 people. Penang Port Commission (PPC) chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin confirmed that a collision involving the ferry Teluk Bahang and the vessel MV Mekar Jaya occurred within the Penang Port limits at 8.40 pm. “The collision occurred between the vessel and the ferry, which was heading to the Sultan Abdul Halim Ferry Terminal.

items.title: Woman injured by falling concrete from heritage building
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A woman in her 20s was injured after concrete debris fell from a heritage building in Lebuh China while crowds were gathering for the Hungry Ghost Festival last night. It is understood that a connecting cable attached to the building's wall became dislodged, causing part of the structure at a corner of the building to detach and fall onto the victim. "I later found out that concrete debris from the building had fallen and struck the woman.

items.title: Germany blames Russia for airport drone incident, hits back with sanctions
items.summary: BERLIN: Germany on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted "hybrid attack" involving an explosive-laden drone at a strategic airport last month and announced diplomatic counter-measures. Germany will close Russia's consulate in the former capital Bonn later this month, and cancel the contract for the Russian House, a cultural centre in Berlin, said Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul. "We are tightening entry controls for Russian nationals" and Germany would propose the listing of more Russian individuals for European Union sanctions, he added, as the Russian ambassador to Berlin was summoned.

items.title: Wall Street ends lower as higher yields, rising oil prices mark shaky start to September
items.summary: NEW YORK: US stocks extended their slide on Tuesday, as the global bond selloff deepened and crude prices spiked amid fading hopes for a near-term solution to the US-Israeli war with Iran. All three major US stock indexes began the month on a sour note, closing decisively lower as rising hostilities in the Middle East drove up oil prices. The benchmark US Treasury yield continued to edge higher after reaching a 19-month high on Monday.

items.title: Families cling to hope as 51 Malaysians remain unreachable after Nepal disaster
items.summary: Let their families see them one last time." Manivannan is the spokesman for Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih), a support group for families of those who have become uncontactable following the disaster. He said the families were growing increasingly worried over the lack of updates from the authorities.

items.title: OpenAI to launch new model with 'stronger safeguards' after hack
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: ChatGPT maker OpenAI said Tuesday it was preparing to release its newest powerful model, known as Astra, after implementing "stronger safeguards" following a rogue cyberattack involving a different AI model. Although Astra "was not involved" in the incident, OpenAI has beefed up its safety measures, the company said in a blog post. That includes classifying Astra as reaching a "critical cybersecurity threshold," which means OpenAI believes the model is capable of finding and exploiting cybersecurity gaps.

items.title: Malaysia risks facing higher US baseline tariff as Washington concludes excess capacity investigation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The United States' 10 per cent baseline tariff on Malaysia's products risks being reviewed if Washington finds that the country has excess industrial capacity, or is being used as a channel for products from countries with excess capacity. The US is expected to announce the findings of its excess-capacity investigation involving Malaysia within three to four weeks, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said yesterday. He said the investigation was nearing completion, with Malaysia continuing to engage US authorities over the definition of excess capacity.

items.title: Asean haze pact still relevant, says Wan Junaidi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar believes that the more than two decades-old Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) is still relevant. However, Wan Junaidi, who served as the natural resources and environment minister from 2015 to 2018, said new technology and methods were needed to tackle the problem. Wan Junaidi also said Malaysia also proposed a plan to fight forest fires.

items.title: OpenAI refutes Apple's trade secret theft claims
items.summary: OPENAI denied Apple's allegations of trade secret theft on Monday, saying the iPhone maker failed to show any confidential information was stolen by former employees. Apple sued OpenAI and former Apple employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu in July, accusing them of misappropriating trade secrets related to hardware design, manufacturing and supply-chain operations as the ChatGPT maker pushes into consumer devices. OpenAI has hired roughly 400 employees from Apple for its hardware initiative, the two companies have written in court filings.

items.title: US strikes Iran in latest tit-for-tat attacks
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US forces launched fresh attacks on Iran Tuesday, including one that the Iranian Red Crescent said left four people dead at a wedding celebration, with Teheran vowing "severe punishment" for the strikes. Washington hit Iranian targets on Sunday in its first known strikes in several weeks, after which Teheran's forces targeted US troops in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, and projectiles struck two oil tankers in unclaimed attacks. Asked if the US military had received any credible reports of civilian casualties from the Tuesday strikes, US Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said "the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC," referring to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

items.title: Sarawak haze could see API levels hit 800, says Wan Junaidi [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: For Sarawak Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, the return of the transboundary haze in Sarawak is a reminder of a problem he spent years trying to resolve. The current episode follows fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, during a prolonged dry period, leaving forests and peatlands vulnerable to fires and winds carrying smoke towards Sarawak. The situation in 2026, especially in Sarawak, is worrying," said Wan Junaidi.

items.title: What Malaysia’s new energy efficiency policy means for your bills, appliances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Malaysia’s new energy-efficiency plan aims to cut energy demand by 11.6 per cent by 2035, while generating RM85 billion in projected energy-cost savings and 815,000 terajoules (TJ) in cumulative energy savings. The projected 815,000 TJ in cumulative energy savings is equivalent to the energy needed to meet Peninsular Malaysia’s entire electricity supply needs for nearly two years, according to the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra). One of the biggest changes under NEEAP 2.0 is that energy efficiency will cover electricity, gas and thermal energy consumption, rather than focusing solely on electricity.

items.title: Hani offers hope to survivors as she prays for miracle
items.summary: Those were the words Hani Othman held on to when she left for Nepal to look for her husband, senior fire officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, who is among a group of 17 Malaysians who became uncontactable following flash floods in the Rasuwa district. Hani, who is now in Kathmandu, told the New Straits Times she did not know how long she would remain in the country. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Ipoh festival to celebrate diverse coffee cultures
items.summary: MALAYSIA's diverse coffee culture, along with food, music and tourism attractions, will be celebrated at the first-ever Ipoh Coffee Vibes festival on Sept 10-13. Loh said the festival would not only highlight the city's signature white coffee but also bring together the coffee cultures of various races. He said participating coffee entrepreneurs would also introduce "Kopi Rakyat" specifically for the festival to allow the public to enjoy various types and flavours of coffee at reasonable prices.

items.title: China's Xi arrives in Egypt as US sanctions threat looms over Iran links
items.summary: CAIRO: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Egypt on Tuesday on a rare trip to the Middle East as both countries face the threat of US sanctions over financial links to Iran. Xi's visit "comes at a time when China's economic interests are directly exposed to the US-Iran war", said Gamal Salama, political science professor at Egypt's Suez University. China is "clearly seeking Egypt's cooperation in managing and shaping regional affairs", said Liu Jia, a research fellow at the Singapore-based Middle East Institute.

items.title: Malaysia, Japan trade rises 12pc
items.summary: He said Japan continues to be one of Malaysia's important trading and investment partners, supported by decades of economic cooperation between the two countries. MAJECA stands for the Malaysia-Japan Economic Association, while JAMECA stands for the Japan-Malaysia Economic Association. Johari said Malaysia is looking to further revitalise and deepen its economic ties with Japan.

items.title: Olympic champ Zheng donates US$150,000 to Nepal-Tibet disaster
items.summary: BEIJING: Olympic tennis champion Zheng Qinwen has donated U$150,000 (RM605,000) to relief efforts following deadly flash floods and landslides that hit the China-Nepal border, a charity said. "(She) will continue to closely monitor the progress of relief efforts, expressing her wishes for fellow compatriots in the disaster zone to overcome difficulties as soon as possible and rebuild their homes," a social media account associated with the China Charity Federation said. Nearly 4,500 people are missing and more than 900 confirmed dead after tsunami-like glacial floods roared down from the border between China's Tibet and Nepal last week.

items.title: 'I thought the ferry was going to sink,' says passenger
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: A passenger feared the ferry would sink after it collided with a vessel in the waters off Penang Port last night. "I was afraid the ferry would sink, but thankfully nothing worse happened," he said when met at the Emergency Department of Seberang Jaya Hospital here last night. Meanwhile, a fellow passenger, known only as Amy Iyana, 23, said she was standing when the collision occurred, causing her to fall backwards and injure her left leg.

items.title: Thailand shortens visa-free stays for dozens of nations from Sept 15
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand will halve the length of visa-free stays for tourists from more than 60 countries and territories to 30 days, effective Sept 15, the foreign ministry said Tuesday. Under Thailand's current tourism scheme, travellers from more than 90 countries – including Europe's 29-nation Schengen area, China, India, the United States and several South American countries – are eligible to visit for up to 60 days without a visa. The reduction to 30 days visa-free applies to over 60 countries and territories, including China, the United States and 27 EU countries, the Thai foreign ministry's consular affairs department said on Tuesday.

items.title: Philippine couple married in hip-deep floodwaters
items.summary: Clutching a bouquet of white blooms and clad in an off-shoulder white gown, Leian Lieza Galang gingerly waded into the murky brown floodwaters inside the Saint John the Baptist church in Hagonoy town, north of Manila, to wed Gilbert Chico. The parish priest declared the couple, both in their 30s, husband and wife at an abbreviated late-morning ceremony, said wedding photographer Mikko Rey Alfonso. Nothing could stop their union," Alfonso said.

items.title: Israeli settlers try to torch West Bank mosque, Palestinians say
items.summary: BAZZARYAH: Israeli settlers tried to set fire to a mosque in the north of the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, Palestinians said, in the latest such attack in the territory. The Palestinian ministry of religious affairs said that "a group of settlers tried to burn parts of the Nur al-Din Zanki Mosque" in Bazzaryah, near Nablus, describing the incident as a "criminal attack." Since the start of 2026, 13 mosques have been "violated" by the Israeli military or settlers, according to the Palestinian ministry of religious affairs.

items.title: Ousted UK PM Starmer quits parliament to focus on international affairs
items.summary: LONDON: Keir Starmer will stand down as a member of parliament, he said on Tuesday, some six weeks after he resigned as Britain's prime minister having lost the support of his Labour Party. Starmer guided Labour into power in 2024 with one of the biggest parliamentary majorities in Britain's modern history, completing a remarkable turnaround having become Labour leader four years earlier after its worst election showing since 1935. Starmer had previously said he would remain as a lawmaker until the next general election.

items.title: Malaysia to host 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting from Sept 7
items.summary: The Health Ministry (MOH), in a Facebook post, said the health meeting will carry the theme, 'Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems'. "Let us together support efforts towards a more equitable, resilient, and future-ready Asean health system," the post read. The conference serves as a vital platform for strengthening public health cooperation and addressing regional health challenges holistically.

items.title: Victoria Bridge access partly closed after child's fatal fall
items.summary: SUNGAI SIPUT: The Victoria Bridge tourist attraction near Enggor here has been temporarily closed following the death of a three-year-old boy who fell about five metres from the bridge. Perak Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said the closure only restricted access to the iron structure of the 100-year-old bridge and did not involve the entire bridge. The 126-year-old Enggor Bridge, better known as Victoria Bridge, is a historic railway bridge in the Karai-Enggor area of Kuala Kangsar.

items.title: Musk defends AI data centres, slams EU rules at G20
items.summary: CHAPEL HILL: Elon Musk on Tuesday urged the G20 to tread softly on regulating tech and AI, saying European-style rules inhibit innovation. Musk also made a defence of building data centres to meet the needs of the AI revolution, amid a growing backlash against their construction in the United States ahead of midterm elections later this year. At the meeting in Chapel Hill, home to the University of North Carolina, a leading US research hub, Musk said the AI data centres were badly needed to fill a "power shortfall" in meeting AI needs.

items.title: Penang ferry collision: Injured toll rises to 21
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Twenty-one people were injured after the Teluk Bahang ferry collided with MV Mekar Jaya within Penang Port limits last night. The Penang Port Commission (PPC) said the incident occurred at about 8.40pm on Sept 1. Yeoh said PPC, together with Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB), would take all necessary measures to ensure appropriate follow-up action for the passengers involved.

items.title: Dialog bags a Aster's crude oil storage tanks job at Singapore's Pulau Bukom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dialog Group Bhd's unit Overseas Technical Engineering and Construction Pte Ltd has bagged a contract from Aster Port & Terminals (APT) to expand crude oil storage tanks at Pulau Bukom in Singapore. Singapore-based PEC Pte Ltd was also awarded a contract by APT for the project, which will increase available crude oil storage capacity at Pulau Bukom by more than 1.3 million barrels, according to a joint statement released by APT. Dialog managing director of engineering, construction and maintenance Bryan Tan said the company would leverage its engineering expertise and construction experience to support APT.

items.title: Pengerang investment must deliver measurable results, financial improvements, says industry expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The multibillion-ringgit investment in Pengerang must now translate into measurable operational and financial improvements, particularly as PRefChem continues to face losses, said industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan. Commenting on a recent report on the financial performance of PRefChem, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd said the performance of the Pengerang Integrated Complex (PIC) should be assessed based on clear and transparent indicators rather than broad assurances. In statement, Jeyenderan said the benefits should extend beyond the financial performance of the complex, particularly in strengthening Malaysia’s domestic fuel security and diversifying crude sourcing.

items.title: Malaysians urged to stay vigilant as Mount Sinabung erupts, flights disrupted, thousands evacuated
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 1 — Malaysians in or travelling to Karo Regency in North Sumatra have been advised to remain vigilant and avoid areas surrounding Mount Sinabung following its eruption on Monday, which disrupted flights and prompted the evacuation of more than 2,400 residents. In a statement on Tuesday, the Consulate General of Malaysia in Medan urged Malaysians to follow instructions issued by the Indonesian authorities, saying several flights at Medan’s Kualanamu International Airport, a key gateway to North Sumatra, had reportedly been rescheduled or cancelled due to volcanic ash. Following the eruption, Indonesia’s Geological Agency raised Mount Sinabung’s status from Level II (Alert) to Level III (Standby) at 12.30pm after visual and instrumental monitoring showed increased volcanic activity.

items.title: Former minister held by MACC to assist Tabung Haji RCI investigation on hotel deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today detained a former minister to assist in investigations in connection with issues raised by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). According to a post on the MACC’s TikTok account, the arrest was linked to an issue involving a hotel lease agreement in Saudi Arabia. Meanwhile, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted, and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Kuching man admits snatching mother’s gold necklace, judge jails him seven years
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — A food delivery rider was sentenced on Tuesday to seven years’ jail and five strokes of the cane for snatching his own mother’s gold necklace. The accused also told police that he committed the act while under the influence of drugs. Background checks by police also showed he had several prior criminal records, including for drugs.

items.title: Visibility stays above minimum at Kuching Airport despite haze, only AirBorneo flights cancelled
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — Operations at Kuching International Airport (KIA) remained largely unaffected despite worsening haze conditions, with only two flights cancelled as visibility in parts of Sarawak deteriorated. KIA senior manager Jun Iskandar Murshidi said the cancelled flights were the Kuching-Mukah and Kuching-Tanjung Manis services, both operated by AirBorneo Airways. “Selected flights are affected due to the worsening haze.

items.title: MOH monitors rise in respiratory infections and conjunctivitis in Sarawak amid haze crisis
items.summary: SIBU, Sept 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is monitoring the increase in cases of acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis in Sarawak following the haze conditions affecting several areas in the state. Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said continuous monitoring is being carried out through health facilities including health clinics and hospitals to ensure that any increase in cases related to the haze can be dealt with immediately. She said based on monitoring by the Sarawak State Health Department (JKN), the average URTI cases increased from about 1,717 cases per week at the beginning of the year to 1,752 cases per week recently.

items.title: Kuala Selangor police say teenager electrocuted after touching lamp post during futsal break
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 1 — A teenage boy died after being electrocuted while holding a lamp post in Taman Pancaran, Bestari Jaya, yesterday. Kuala Selangor police chief Supt Azaharudin Tajuddin said they received a call regarding the incident involving the 15-year-old boy at about 10.32pm. “The Kuala Selangor District Police Headquarters Operations Room received a call regarding a boy who was found unconscious and believed to be dead.

items.title: ‘Literally tasting the smoke’: Sarawakians suffer as haze worsens
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — Air quality in Malaysia's Sarawak state deteriorated further today as smoke from Indonesian forest fires drove up respiratory complaints and sent residents scrambling for protective masks. Six districts in Sarawak, on Borneo, recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, including the state capital, Kuching, where the API hit 407. Mason said the worsening air had also affected her health, causing a sore throat and aggravating her asthma.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, ex-Treasury sec-gen released from MACC custody in RCI-linked probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and a former Treasury secretary-general were reportedly released from Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) custody today in an investigation linked to a royal commission of inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrims’ fund. The politician and former TH chairman and the former Finance Ministry official were arrested at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on August 26. Before that, MACC detained seven people comprising a shipping company chief executive officer, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.

items.title: Ayer Itam brawl involved Geng 04 members in debt dispute, Penang police say
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have confirmed that an armed fight that caused two individuals to suffer severe injuries in front of a National Type Chinese Primary School in Ayer Itam here on Saturday involved Geng 04 members. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said all 13 men arrested to facilitate investigations into the case are believed to be members of the same gang but in different areas and the fight was due to a misunderstanding over debts. He said the two severely injured men, in their 30s, were not gang members but were attacked when they were misidentified as suspects involved in the fight, adding the victims were on their way back from a religious festival when they were attacked by the group.

items.title: Three-year-old boy found dead below Victoria Bridge in Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 1 — A three-year-old boy was reportedly found dead on a road beneath the Victoria Bridge in Enggor here yesterday evening. Sinar Harian reported that Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim was taken to Kuala Kangsar Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at about 7.40pm. The Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council subsequently cordoned off the bridge with safety tape.

items.title: Penang police arrest married couple, two others in drug syndicate on Thai intel tip
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have arrested four members of an international drug syndicate, including a married couple, and seized 86 kilogrammes of methamphetamine worth RM4.31 million in a series of raids in Selangor and Penang recently. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the success was the result of intelligence sharing between the Royal Malaysia Police and the Royal Thai Police after Thai authorities arrested a Malaysian man in Hua Hin, Thailand, on Aug 8. Thai narcotics police conducted an investigation and obtained intelligence, which was subsequently shared with the Malaysian Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID).

items.title: Duta Enclave: Court told RM1.39m payout to Semantan Estate was more than adequate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, September 1 — The High Court was told today that the RM1.39 million in compensation paid by the Government of Malaysia to Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 was more than adequate. “I have prepared an expert valuation report to determine adequate compensation, in accordance with the Court of Appeal Order dated June 24, 2025, which, among others, fixed the valuation date for determining compensation for the said land as December 3, 1956. “Given that the government had previously paid compensation of $1,390,602.70 (in 1956) to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate), that amount exceeds the compensation I recommended under Valuation Basis 1.

items.title: Former PM Muhyiddin, ‘Azman’ and ‘Adam’ listed in same July 2020 golf game at Tropicana, witness tells court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin played in a golf game in July 2020 at Tropicana Golf Club with 14 other players, including two individuals identified as “Azman” and “Adam”, Tropicana Golf & Country Resort Berhad (TGCRB) employee Saravanan Subaramaniam told the High Court today. TGCRB group head of security Saravanan said this while testifying as the 28th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial. Saravanan said Tropicana Golf Club’s digital golf registration system showed that Muhyiddin and the 14 other individuals had played there in four “flights”, or groups, on July 19, 2020, with a single invoice issued for all 15 players.

items.title: Juwai IQI: Malaysia among top destinations for Chinese property buyers, investment on track to top RM1.6b a year
items.summary: According to new insights released today by Juwai IQI, the profile of Chinese buyers in Malaysia is undergoing a significant transformation. “Malaysia is now the fourth most popular destination for Chinese property buyers, up from sixth in 2025 and from seventh in 2022, 2023, and 2024,” Kashif said. In 2024, Malaysia attracted 2.8 per cent of global property enquiries from Chinese homebuyers, with the figure climbing to 4.5 per cent in 2025.

items.title: Perak assembly to choose new senator between PKR and PAS nominees
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — The upcoming Perak State Legislative Assembly sitting will see a motion tabled to elect a new senator, Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said. Mohammad Zahir said the motion would be tabled by Mentri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad. He also said two Bills would be tabled during the sitting, namely the Administrative Members and State Assembly Members (Salary) Enactment 2026 and the Islamic Religious Administration (Perak) (Amendment) Enactment 2026.

items.title: Deadly LPT1 pile-up: Four dead include family returning from National Day parade in Putrajaya
items.summary: Mohd Kazwan Mohd Kassim, 59, the father of one of the victims, Nur Atiqah Sofiya, 32, said it was the first time his daughter, her husband, Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi, 32, and their son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, four, had celebrated National Day in Putrajaya. Meanwhile, the victim’s cousin, Nur Awatif Adawiyah Abdul Aziz, 30, said Nur Atiqah Sofiya had sent photos of the National Day celebrations to the family’s WhatsApp group and also uploaded photos to her Instagram Story. We never thought these photos would become their last memories,” she said.

items.title: Court of Appeal allows Rosmah to introduce new evidence in solar graft appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Court of Appeal today allowed applications by former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction, paving the way for the evidence to be heard by the High Court. A three-member panel comprising Justices Choo Kah Sing, Azhahari Kamal Ramli and K. Muniandy allowed both applications before it and ordered that the additional evidence be taken before another High Court judge. Justice Choo, who read the panel’s decision, said the court was satisfied that the requirements for admitting the additional evidence had been met.

items.title: Sabah disaster committee urges public to limit outdoor activities as four districts record unhealthy API
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 1 — The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) has urged the public, particularly vulnerable groups, to limit outdoor activities and avoid strenuous physical exertion after four locations across the state recorded unhealthy air pollutant index (API) levels today. The committee issued the advisory as hazy conditions shrouded several districts, calling on children, senior citizens, pregnant women, and individuals suffering from respiratory illnesses to exercise extra caution. The advisory comes as data from the Sabah Department of Environment (DOE) showed air quality worsening across multiple monitoring stations as of 8am today.

items.title: Islamic affairs minister denounces Malaysian’s participation in Bangkok transgender pageant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) has strongly condemned the participation of an individual, allegedly representing Malaysia, in a transgender beauty pageant held in Bangkok last Sunday. “Religious authorities will work with the relevant agencies to examine possible action under existing laws,” he said. Earlier, a video showing an individual representing Malaysia at an international transgender beauty pageant went viral on social media, drawing mixed reactions from netizens.

items.title: ‘Baddestcoach’ defamation suit against Caprice heads to trial after settlement talks collapse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The defamation suit filed by renowned high-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Murad “Baddestcoach” Zaidi, against social media influencer Caprice will proceed to full trial following the failure of both parties to reach an amicable settlement at the High Court here. He added that the mediation proceedings, which took place on July 31 and lasted nearly four hours, were attended by both Caprice, whose real name is Ariz Ramli, and Murad Zaidi. On Nov 8 last year, the High Court recorded a consent order compelling Caprice to immediately remove and withdraw nine defamatory statements published on his Instagram account against Murad Zaidi.

items.title: Sarawak electoral boundary redelineation: 17 new seats proposed, 10 renamed
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — Seventeen new state constituencies have been proposed across Sarawak under the Election Commission’s (EC) 2026 electoral boundary review, with Petra Jaya, Sibu, and Miri parliamentary constituencies each set to gain two new seats. Miri would also gain two new constituencies through the proposed Permaisuri and Tudan. In addition, the EC has proposed changes to the names of 10 state constituencies.

items.title: No changes to Perak Opposition seating despite Bersatu fallout, says Speaker
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — The Perak State Assembly has not received any formal request to alter the Opposition’s seating arrangement following recent sackings and suspensions within Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said today. In June, Sungai Manik assemblyman Datuk Zainol Fadzi Paharudin announced his entry into Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), four months after his expulsion from Bersatu. Zainol Fadzi was among 17 members sacked nationwide by Bersatu over alleged party sabotage.

items.title: Penang DVS: No clear offence under Animal Welfare Act for owner failing to stop dog fight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Animal Welfare Act 2015 contains no clear provision making it an offence for a dog owner to fail to intervene when dogs fight, the Penang Veterinary Services Department (DVS) has said. “There is no clear provision under the Act that (makes it) an offence by an owner for an animal fight or for failing to stop the fight,” DVS was quoted as saying. However, it said action could be considered under Section 8 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 if there was evidence that someone had encouraged or prompted an animal to attack, alarm or frighten another person or animal.

items.title: Johari Ghani: US forced labour issue resolved, excess capacity still pending
items.summary: He said the investigation is close to being finalised, while Malaysia continues to engage with the US on the definition of excess capacity. “They have almost finalised the excess capacity investigation. Johari said Malaysia’s concern is that the US definition of excess capacity also takes into account capacity originating from third countries.
